title: Mid-Year English Assessment
description: Review your English progress with a mid-year assessment covering grammar, vocabulary, reading, listening, writing and speaking.
learning_objectives: Practise short writing and speaking tasks

body_markdown:
## 1. How to take this assessment

Complete the questions without looking at the answers. For the listening section, ask someone to read the passage aloud or use text-to-speech. Writing and speaking tasks are self-assessed.

## 2. Grammar and vocabulary

Choose the correct answer.

1. She ______ to work every day. (go / goes / going)
2. I ______ studying now. (am / is / are)
3. They ______ at home yesterday. (was / were / are)
4. He did not ______ the message. (receive / received / receives)
5. We will ______ tomorrow. (meet / met / meeting)
6. The book is ______ the table. (in / on / at)
7. I need ______ umbrella. (a / an / the)
8. Choose the opposite of “early”. (late / soon / quick)
9. Choose the synonym of “begin”. (start / stop / finish)
10. A person who works with you is a ______. (colleague / customer / stranger)

## 3. Reading comprehension

Read this passage:

“Neha works in a small office. She usually reaches work at nine. Every morning, she checks her emails and prepares a task list. Yesterday, she attended a meeting with her team. They discussed a new project and decided to begin it next Monday.”

Answer:

11. Where does Neha work?
12. What does she check every morning?
13. What did the team discuss?
14. When will the new project begin?

## 4. Listening comprehension

Ask someone to read this passage aloud:

“Ramesh is going to visit his uncle this Sunday. He will travel by train. He has already booked his ticket and plans to leave home early.”

15. Who is Ramesh going to visit?
16. How will he travel?
17. What has he already booked?

## 5. Writing task

Write a paragraph of six to eight sentences on “How I use English in daily life”. Check spelling, capital letters, full stops and sentence structure.

## 6. Speaking task

Speak for two minutes about your work, studies or daily routine. Include an introduction, three details and a closing sentence.

## 7. Answer key

1. goes; 2. am; 3. were; 4. receive; 5. meet; 6. on; 7. an; 8. late; 9. start; 10. colleague.

11. In a small office; 12. Her emails; 13. A new project; 14. Next Monday; 15. His uncle; 16. By train; 17. His ticket.

## 8. Score guide

- 14–17: Strong progress. Continue practising all four skills.
- 10–13: Good foundation. Review missed topics.
- 6–9: Revisit grammar, vocabulary and reading lessons.
- 0–5: Return to beginner lessons and practise step by step.

Writing and speaking are not included in the 17 objective answers. Review them separately for clarity, accuracy and organisation.

faq.question: How many objective questions are included?
faq.answer: There are 17 objective questions across grammar, vocabulary, reading and listening.

faq.question: Are writing and speaking included in the score?
faq.answer: They are separate self-assessment tasks. Review them for clarity, accuracy and organisation.

faq.question: What should I do after the assessment?
faq.answer: Review the topics you found difficult and practise them before taking the assessment again.
